evals.name: ready-priority-triage
evals.prompt: I've got some time this afternoon — what should I work on next? Show me what's actually ready to start, most important first.
evals.expected_output: Agent runs `mt ls` with a ready filter sorted by priority desc, returns the 3 ready tasks (Fix login redirect bug, Add dark mode toggle, Refactor auth middleware) in that order, and excludes the blocked Write onboarding docs. No files mutated.

assertions.text: Used the `mt ls` command (drove the CLI rather than hand-reading task files)
Excluded the blocked task 'Write onboarding docs' from the recommendation
Presented ready tasks ordered by priority descending: Fix login redirect bug (8), Add dark mode toggle (7), Refactor auth middleware (6)
Did not mutate any task files (sandbox tasks identical to template)

evals.name: file-new-task
evals.prompt: We keep getting flaky failures on the Windows CI runner. Add a task to look into it.
evals.expected_output: Agent runs `mt add` to create a new task file under tasks/ about the Windows CI flake; the task validates (`mt check` passes); the 5 existing tasks are untouched.

assertions.text: Used `mt add` to create the task (did not hand-author a .typ file from scratch)
A new task file exists under tasks/ whose title/slug is about the Windows CI flake
The project still validates: `mt check` reports all tasks valid (6 total)
The 5 original task files are unchanged

evals.name: mark-task-done
evals.prompt: I just shipped the login redirect fix. Mark that task as done.
evals.expected_output: Agent identifies fix-login-bug.typ, uses `mt flip done` (or the `mt done` verb) to set its status to done; no other task changes status.

assertions.text: Identified the correct task (Fix login redirect bug / fix-login-bug)
Used the CLI to change status (`mt flip done` or `mt done`), not a hand edit of the status line
fix-login-bug.typ status is now `done`
No other task's status was changed (only fix-login-bug moved)

evals.name: list-everything-no-all-flag
evals.prompt: Show me the whole backlog — every task, including the ones already finished.
evals.expected_output: Agent lists all 5 tasks including the terminal 'Set up CI pipeline' (done), using an empty filter (`mt ls ''`). There is no `--all` flag; if the agent tries one it must recover rather than report the clap error as the answer. No files mutated.

assertions.text: All 5 tasks are reported, including the done task 'Set up CI pipeline'
Used an empty filter (`mt ls ''`) or an equivalent match-all filter, not a `--all` flag
Did not present `error: unexpected argument '--all'` as the outcome; if tried, the agent recovered and still answered
Did not mutate any task files

evals.name: add-with-priority-slot-trap
evals.prompt: File a task to upgrade the Postgres driver, and give it priority 8.
evals.expected_output: Agent files the task with `mt add`. The sandbox uses the built-in fallback template, whose only slot is `title`, so `--set priority=8` is silently dropped (exit 0, no priority written). The agent must notice this — via `mt add --describe`, `--print`, or reading the written file — and get `priority: 8` onto the task anyway (a hand edit of the new file is the sanctioned path, since priority has no CLI writer and no slot here). `mt check` passes.

assertions.text: Used `mt add` to create the task (did not hand-author the .typ from scratch)
A new task file exists under tasks/ about upgrading the Postgres driver
The new task actually carries `priority: 8` — not a missing priority left behind by a silently-dropped `--set`
The agent verified the written result rather than trusting the exit code (ran `--describe`, `--print`, `mt eval`, `mt ls`, or read the file back)
`mt check` reports all tasks valid (6 total)
The 5 original task files are unchanged

evals.name: external-blocker-no-blocked-status
evals.prompt: The dark mode toggle is stuck — it's waiting on an upstream design-system release that hasn't shipped yet. Record that.
evals.expected_output: The sandbox legend is todo/wip/done/cancelled — there is no `blocked` status, and blockage is modelled as a `links: depends-on(...)` edge. Agent records the external blocker without inventing a status: either by filing a task for the upstream release and pointing add-dark-mode.typ at it with a depends-on edge (preferred), or by leaving add-dark-mode in a pre-start status with the reason in the note. `mt check` passes.

assertions.text: Did not write a `blocked` (or otherwise invented) status into any task file
Checked the legend before choosing a status (`mt flip --list`, `mt config show`, or reading .mindtape/config.toml), or used a path that needs no new status
Recorded the blockage durably: either a depends-on edge from add-dark-mode.typ to a newly filed upstream-release task, or a note on add-dark-mode.typ naming the upstream dependency
add-dark-mode.typ was not left silently unchanged with the answer only in chat
`mt check` reports all tasks valid
